clue.text: Superlative ending in quintet is joyous

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

parts.note: a quintet is a group of five
the suffix that forms superlatives, as in biggest

explanation.surface: A musical review: the closing movement of a quintet was the happiest moment of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superlative ending' is not the finale of a performance but the suffix that ends words like biggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive describes the cheerful mood of a celebration, a near synonym of joyous.

clue.text: Body part receiving attention in class

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it in, holding it inside

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
to lend an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A pupil's body part getting looked at during a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm is the part of the arm between elbow and wrist.

clue.text: Struck with small glove

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Someone was hit with a small glove, as in a challenge to a duel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck' reads as hit, and smitten is indeed the old past participle of smite.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the past participle of smite, so it means struck, as well as infatuated.

clue.text: Perfect statement from one giving everyone a hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flawless, the best possible

definitions.text: statement from one giving everyone a hand
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a card dealer announces before dealing to each player, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving everyone a hand' sounds like helping or applauding, but it is dealing cards; the dealer's words split as I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly right, and read as two words it is a card dealer's announcement.

clue.text: Fanatic's taken out of context re mistake

indicators.note: taken out of means the letters are lifted from inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters starting inside the first word and ending inside the last

explanation.surface: A zealot's words quoted out of context, which the clue calls a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical views and pursues them zealously, which is what a fanatic does.

clue.text: Counsellor is taken in by part of speech, almost

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it
almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an adverb is one of the parts of speech
taken as written

explanation.surface: A counsellor is drawn into a grammar lesson that almost finishes covering a part of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsellor' is spelt here with -ER; the -OR spelling is also common but would not fit the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser is someone who gives counsel professionally, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bishops, in old-fashioned agreement, upset church

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards
the bishops sitting in the other word are placed inside it

parts.note: yea is an archaic word for yes
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Bishops, agreeing in an outdated way, have caused trouble for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a church that belongs, or once belonged, to a monastery.

clue.text: Note always put in travel document? Just the opposite

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a visa is an entry permit stamped in a passport
C is a musical note
ever means always

explanation.surface: A note is always slipped into a travel document, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a phrase, not a single word, and the surface itself asks which goes in which.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is a Latin phrase meaning the other way round, with the order reversed.

clue.text: Thus article is about one African country or another

definitions.note: read with the clue's 'African country': another one

indicators.note: a word that is about another wraps around it

parts.note: so means thus
Mali is a West African nation
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article seems to be about an African country, or maybe a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: one African country builds the clue, and the answer is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a nation on the Horn of Africa, a second African country beside the one in the wordplay.

clue.text: Begin afresh with skill after break

parts.note: a rest is a break
an art is a skill

explanation.surface: Coming back fresh and skilful after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the skill second.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start again from the beginning, the same as beginning afresh.

clue.text: Object wrapped in torn old clothes

indicators.note: something wrapped in another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: rent is an old past tense of rend, to tear
an object or goal is an aim

explanation.surface: Some item has been bundled up in tattered old garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: raiment is a dated, literary word for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic term for garments, so 'old clothes' describes the word itself.

clue.text: Changes into suits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turns into, as a caterpillar turns into a butterfly
second meaning: looks good on, flatters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting dressed in formal suits; the clue is really two separate meanings of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to grow into something new and to flatter someone's appearance, as a hat does.

clue.text: Weapons poorly positioned in vessel carrying vital supply

indicators.note: something positioned in a word is set inside it

parts.note: a blood vessel carrying the body's essential blood supply
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: Guns badly sited aboard a ship that carries essential provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel; ILL goes in after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large guns, so it names a body of weapons.

clue.text: Country house I will set in very limited area

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the surrounding letters

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
the contraction I'll, without its apostrophe
area cut down to its abbreviation A

explanation.surface: Someone vows to build a country house on a very small plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' tells you to shorten the words around it to abbreviations, V and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country residence, especially one in Italy or the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Painter, male and French

parts.note: a man is a male
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: Describes an artist as a Frenchman, which the real Manet was.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of the painter, but 'and French' asks for the French word for and.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French painter, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Score I put together in game

parts.note: a score is twenty
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A player's totting up their points in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: in this card game the score you aim for is twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-one is the card game also called blackjack or pontoon.

clue.text: Replacing fellow artist, finally, as singer?

parts.note: a substitute comes in for someone: IN FOR
a fellow is a man

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of artist

explanation.surface: A singer is brought in as a stand-in for another performer.
explanation.walkthrough: In slang, to sing is to give information to the police, so the singer is a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal slang says an informer 'sings' when telling the police what they know, so an informant is a singer.

clue.text: It signals danger with shooter crossing a line

indicators.note: a word crossing others spans them, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a shooter is slang for a gun
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A gunman crossing a boundary is a warning sign of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters go in after FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a bell or siren that warns people of a fire.

clue.text: Rich high-flier? Stone me!

parts.note: jet is a black stone used in jewellery
the setter of the crossword is the 'me' writing the clue

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a wealthy, high-living person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' is a British exclamation of astonishment; here it splits into a stone and the crossword's author.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy person who flies around the world for pleasure, literally a high-flier.

clue.text: Good-humoured jest initially related to sightseers?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of jest
sightseers read literally as eyes, which see sights; ocular means relating to the eyes

explanation.surface: A joke at the start of a tour, aimed at the tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sightseers' means tourists on the surface but eyes in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular means joking and playful, so it describes a good-humoured manner.

clue.text: Exercised short time, then showered

parts.note: time shortened to its abbreviation T
showers are light rain

explanation.surface: Someone worked out briefly, then had a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To have trained is to have exercised, as an athlete does in preparation.

clue.text: Present, a tie, sent back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sent back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tie in a match is a draw

explanation.surface: A gift necktie has been returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' and 'tie' suggest a gift of neckwear; the tie is a drawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: To award is to present someone with a prize, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Person's bad reaction largely misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's bad reaction was mostly out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' reads as mostly, which suggests dropping letters, but all seven are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body's adverse response to a substance such as pollen.

clue.text: Celebrity framed by parent as scoundrel

indicators.note: a picture framed by something is enclosed on all sides

parts.note: a dad is a parent
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A famous person set up by their own father, who is a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' suggests a false accusation, but it simply puts one word around another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a mean, cowardly villain.

clue.text: Religious singing in church, then a part of Bible

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written
the New Testament, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: A service where the congregation sings, followed by a reading from Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a sung liturgical text, such as plainsong, so it is a kind of religious singing.

clue.text: Indicate some Europeans as upholders of standards

parts.note: to flag something is to point it out
Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Pointing out certain Europeans as guardians of moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' are flags, not principles, which is why the definition raises a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and a flagpole literally holds a flag up.

clue.text: Discover with concealed drug, hence punished, in a way

indicators.note: having something concealed means holding it hidden inside

parts.note: to discover is to find
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Caught with hidden drugs and so penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' is fair because a fine is only one kind of punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fined means being punished by having to pay money, one particular form of penalty.

clue.text: Having no faith in search for metals, including silver

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one word holds another

parts.note: prospectors pan for gold by washing gravel
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A faithless prospector hunting for gold and silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: pagan strictly means outside the main religions, often heathen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan describes someone outside the major faiths, loosely irreligious or a heathen.

clue.text: Union leader shot in dramatic circumstances

definitions.text: Union leader shot in dramatic circumstances

parts.note: surface reading: a trade union boss gunned down in a dramatic incident
setter's reading: the president who led the Union in the American Civil War, assassinated while watching a play at Ford's Theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic' is literal: the shooting happened in a theatre during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln led the Union side in the Civil War and was shot at a theatre in 1865.

clue.text: Regalia adapted for country on Med

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal insignia modified for use in a Mediterranean state.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation with a long Mediterranean coastline.

clue.text: E.g. diamond put on table first, source of bright colour

parts.note: diamonds are a red suit in cards
in card games, to lead is to play the first card

explanation.surface: A card player opens with a diamond, laying it down first.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture is consistent: diamonds are red, and playing first is leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Red lead is a bright orange-red lead oxide used as a pigment and in paint.

clue.text: Doctor, new, observed to be rich

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
N is the abbreviation for new
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A newly qualified doctor is seen to be wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having plenty of money, the same as wealthy.
